messages:
stephen_support: FYI customer reported a regression after upgrading redwood-python from 1.27.x -> 1.28.0. Their app used the `stop` param and now it's apparently being ignored, causing much longer outputs and higher token spend. attaching repro.
raj_support: ugh. do we have a quick repro? can you paste the minimal snippet and pip commands?
stephen_support: sure — steps they ran: ```bash
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install redwood==1.28.0
# run script below
```
and the script: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = client.generate(prompt="Write me a haiku", stop=["\n\n"], max_tokens=10)
print(resp.text)
```
Output: long poem, >150 tokens. With 1.27.3 the output respects `stop` and ends ~8 tokens.
alex_platform: can repro locally with 1.28.0, confirmed stop list ignored when provided as list (strange). single-string stop works.
morgan_pm: is this new behavior intentional? any deprecation notes?
stephen_support: release notes mention param rename `stop_sequences`->`stop` in 1.28 but not that list shapes changed. customer says they didn't change callsite.
raj_support: quick workaround: pin to 1.27.3 — can we recommend that to affected customers immediately?
alex_platform: yes, pin to 1.27.3 restores previous behavior. also adding a server-side regression test for list stop values.
raj_support: creating a support reply: "Temporary workaround: pin redwood==1.27.3. We're escalating to engineering for a patch. Sorry for the disruption" :thumbsup:
stephen_support: pasted repro logs: ``ERROR`` not thrown, function returns 200 with full text. stack trace shows new signature dispatch path hitting `_normalize_stop()` in client v1.28 which treats lists as tokens not sequences.
morgan_pm: escalate to eng-runtime, assign priority P1 (billing impact).
alex_platform: on it. I can prepare a 1.28.1 rollback/patch — likely a one-line fix in input normalization to accept list[str].
deploy-bot: Deployment window suggested: immediate hotfix-staging -> canary-prod after tests clear.
raj_support: I'll notify customer and advise pin. also asking for estimate: how long to patch?
alex_platform: patch + tests + canary ~ 4-6 hours if nothing else blocks. will post PR.
stephen_support: customer replied: "thank you — pin applied, rolling back now. appreciate the fast response."
morgan_pm: please add a changelog note and retrospective to avoid silent parameter suppression in future. this bit bit us (billing exposure).
ale
x_platform: adding a failing unit test to repro then push PR, will @raj when merged.
raj_support: resolved for now — keeping thread open until patch is live. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
